Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
342 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Updated discussion for Key Messages 1 and 2.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Sharply cooler conditions are expected through midweek.

2) A storm system likely impacts the area Thursday into Friday 
with rain, strong winds, and widespread coastal flooding.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Cold frontal passage this afternoon is ushering in a sharply 
cooler air mass into the region for midweek.

After days of unseasonably mild afternoons, temperatures on
Tuesday struggle to hit 50 despite abundant sunshine, with most
topping out in the upper 40s. This sets up the coldest night of
the season so far for most Tuesday night with areas outside of 
the NYC metro falling below the freezing mark, and even the city
dropping into the mid 30s. Similar conditions can be expected 
on Wednesday, though cloud cover begins to increase in the
afternoon ahead of approaching low pressure from the south.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
An impactful storm system is increasingly likely to move through on 
Thanksgiving and bring rain, wind, and coastal flood concerns.

An anomalously strong 1040+ mb high in place over the Northeast
midweek will lead to a tight pressure gradient as deepening 
surface low pressure drives north into the Mid Atlantic. An 
associated potent 60-70 kt LLJ at 925 mb moves overhead by 
Thursday night and wind headlines may eventually be needed, 
especially along the coast where winds will be strongest. As it
looks now, widespread sustained E/NE winds 15-25 mph develop by
late Thursday morning, with gusts peaking 35-45 mph during the 
afternoon and the evening. Depending on the strength and 
position of the synoptic features, wind gusts could exceed 50 
mph along the coast for a period.

A period of steady moderate, locally heavy, rainfall is expected
sometime Thursday into Thursday night. Differences in timing 
still need to be resolved, with the GFS-GEFS-AIGFS notably 
faster than the EC-EPS-AIFS by 6 to 12 hours. Between these 
camps, the rain could develop as early as Thursday morning, or 
as late as early Thursday evening. Ensemble means are averaging 
between 1 and 2 inches, with localized higher amounts toward 3 
inches or so possible. WPC continues to maintain a marginal risk
of excessive rainfall for the entire region. While localized 
flash floods can't be ruled out, much more likely is the minor, 
nuisance type flooding in urbanized and poor drainage environments.
Freshwater flooding impacts look limited due to the progressive
nature of the system.

Coastal flooding is also growing more likely with a full moon on the 
24th and king tides this week. Given high astrotides, many locations 
need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood benchmarks. 
Localized minor coastal flooding is possible with Wednesday 
morning's high tide. Then, the current forecast supports widespread 
minor to moderate flooding Thursday morning through Friday morning. 
Localized major is a possibility for the most vulnerable locations 
of the south shore back bays and western Great South Bay. There are 
also a few spots in NE NJ such as Kearney Point and Hackensack River 
that are being watched for localized major coastal flooding. Some 
guidance, such as Stevens, has increased the potential for localized 
major flooding. In the end, this will be determined by how fast the 
low tracks up the coast and how far inland of a track it takes. This 
will determine just how long we stay in E/NE flow before switching 
over to S/SW. In addition, beach flooding, erosion, and overwash 
would all be on the table. For now, the risk of overwash appears 
isolated, but this could change depending on how the system
trends. 

Given the event is still several days days out, there remains a
fair amount of spread in guidance with the evolution of the 
system. Continue to monitor the forecast for updates on potential
impacts.

A cold frontal passage occurs this afternoon. 

VFR thru the TAF period.

Wind shift to the NW behind the front this aftn. Some gusts to
20kt possible, then a tendency towards lighter winds tngt. Winds
increase on Tue in the 15-25kt range.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Tuesday through Saturday... 

Rest of Tuesday: VFR. NW winds diminishing winds aft 00Z.

Wednesday: VFR with winds becoming NE. 

Thanksgiving: Rain developing with IFR. E winds 15-25kt
G30-40kt. Peak gusts potentially higher. LLWS possible with 
50+kt at 1000ft.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory continues on the nearshore ocean waters and
LI Sound east of the CT River with seas around or just above 5 
ft. Seas subside on eastern Sound tonight, but SCA conditions 
may persist on the ocean through much of Tuesday with seas near 
5 ft and wind gusts toward 25 kt developing in the afternoon. 
Conditions should finally abate on all waters by Tuesday evening.

A brief lull in SCA conditions is then expected into Wednesday 
before conditions start to ramp up Wednesday night ahead of an 
approaching low pressure from the south. Gale conditions are 
likely on all waters, with potential of storm force on the ocean
Thursday through Thursday evening. Max significant wave heights
could reach up to 15-20 ft on the ocean and occasionally to 
20-25 ft out east, 7-10 ft across LI Sound and around 10 ft on 
western Block Island Sound E of Orient Point. Gales may continue
into Friday as the storm departs to the north.
